original_question: Fix a prime p and integers r <= s. Assuming p^r Br(F) is generated by cyclic algebras, what is the minimal number l_F(p^r, p^s) such that every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r is Brauer-equivalent to a tensor product of that many cyclic algebras of degree p^r?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target very closely: it fixes a prime p and integers r <= s; it uses the cyclic-generation hypothesis on the p^r-torsion in the Brauer group; it asks for the invariant l_F(p^r,p^s); and it correctly unpacks l_F(p^r,p^s) as the least number of cyclic factors of degree p^r needed to represent every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r up to Brauer equivalence/similarity. This is exactly the content of Problem 3.5 once the notation is made explicit.
missing_details: The paper's ambient object is a field F; this should be stated explicitly.
The torsion notation should be made explicit as the p^r-torsion subgroup of the Brauer group, usually written _{p^r}Br(F), rather than the ambiguous string "p^r Br(F)".

The paper defines l_F(m,n) only after introducing the general setup: m and n have the same prime factors, m divides n, and _mBr(F) is generated by cyclic algebras; your draft jumps directly to the prime-power specialization.
The paper's definition includes the convention that if no uniform bound exists, then l_F(m,n) = infinity; your draft omits this.
The paper phrases the representation as "similar to a tensor product"; to be fully stand-alone, it helps to say explicitly that this is equivalent to Brauer-equivalent in this context.
The paper's official formulation is an open problem to "compute" l_F(p^r,p^s), not merely to define the invariant.
refined_question: Let F be a field, let p be a prime, and let integers r <= s be given. Assume that the p^r-torsion subgroup _{p^r}Br(F) of the Brauer group is generated by classes of cyclic algebras. Define l_F(p^r,p^s) to be the least integer l such that every central simple F-algebra of degree p^s and period dividing p^r is similar (equivalently, Brauer-equivalent) to a tensor product of l cyclic F-algebras of degree p^r; if no such uniform bound exists, set l_F(p^r,p^s)=infinity. Compute l_F(p^r,p^s).
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at the symbol-length problem in Section 3, not at the paper's Section 1 problems. The exact nearest formulation is Problem 3.5, which in the paper reads: for a prime p and integers r <= s, under the hypothesis that the p^r-torsion in Br(F) is generated by cyclic algebras, compute l_F(p^r,p^s). The surrounding paragraph immediately before Problem 3.5 supplies the full definition of l_F(m,n): it is the least number of cyclic algebras of degree m whose tensor product represents every central simple F-algebra of degree n and period dividing m, with the convention l_F(m,n)=infinity if no such bound exists. The background section provides the needed stand-alone meaning of Brauer equivalence/similarity. So your draft is essentially correct, but it needs the field F, the precise torsion notation, the infinity convention, and the paper's terminology "similar" made explicit.
